evals.prompt: Add @mrpvi/fluentui-vue to an existing Vue 3.5 TypeScript app. Show the entry file and a complete App.vue with a primary button and one section using the dark Fluent theme. State the checks you would run. Do not change files; return code and brief notes.
evals.expected_output: Root imports, one shared stylesheet import, valid FButton registration, a fui-theme-dark ancestor, and consumer checks without a React provider.
assertions: Exactly one shared stylesheet import is shown across the entry and App.vue.
FButton is imported from @mrpvi/fluentui-vue and uses appearance=primary.
The dark section has a fui-theme-dark ancestor and does not use a React FluentProvider.
The answer identifies consumer typecheck/build and keyboard checks without claiming they ran.

evals.prompt: In a Vue 3.5 application using @mrpvi/fluentui-vue, build a labelled required customer-name field and a multi-select combobox of related customers. Keep stored customer IDs separate from typed search text. Return a complete Vue SFC with initialized state and briefly explain controlled versus default state. The shared stylesheet is already imported.
evals.expected_output: FField/FInput composition, labelled combobox, string text model and string-array selected-options model, explicit option value/text, and correct controlled/default guidance.
assertions: The required customer-name FField wraps FInput in its default slot.
The combobox has a label and binds string text through v-model separately from a string[] v-model:selected-options.
FOption has a stored value and explicit human-readable text.
The answer distinguishes initialized controlled refs from uncontrolled default props and does not mix both for one channel.

evals.prompt: Using @mrpvi/fluentui-vue in Vue 3.5, show a menu action that opens a dialog and a toast after a simulated successful save. Return complete parent/child SFCs if needed. Avoid nested buttons; explain keyboard/focus checks. The shared stylesheet is already imported.
evals.expected_output: Correct menu and dialog roots/parts, native trigger semantics, toaster ancestor with descendant controller injection, dialog kept outside the dismissed menu subtree, and a stable focus-return plan.
assertions: Menu and dialog parts have the corresponding root ancestors, with the dialog outside the dismissing menu subtree.
Native trigger buttons contain no nested buttons and the menu trigger uses type=button.
useToastController runs in a descendant component of FToaster and dispatchToast receives content followed by options.
For the checked package version, FDialogSurface mounts conditionally with the open model so focus registration works on first open and reopen.
The answer supplies a stable focus-return plan and explicitly checks keyboard handoff, Tab containment, and Escape.
